answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with work-backed reputation that grows like a spiral: a new identity starts with zero trust and earns it only by completing verified tasks for established peers, each attestation adding a small step upward. Fake accounts echo each other, but their endorsements carry no weight because they hold no earned stake, and one proven cedar of real completed work outweighs a forest of empty clones. Creating thousands of identities costs time and compute yet buys no trust, so attackers pay more than they gain.
